variant.name: command-signals
variant.hypothesis: Explicitly favor the compact signals view for command results when the agent only needs execution outcomes, increasing command savings without affecting edit recall.

prompts.viewInstructions: A coding agent working on `task` just called `agent.tool` with `agent.args` (its reasoning right before the call is `agent.text_before_call`). The output is large. Which view is the smallest one that still gives the agent everything needed for its next step? For command output, choose signals when errors, warnings, tests, or the final summary are sufficient; choose full when exact output, copying, or details anywhere are needed. For other output, prefer smaller views only when the agent's purpose is clearly served; when in doubt, choose full.

viewDescriptions.signals: Command output reduced to errors, warnings, failing tests, and final summary lines with context, line-numbered. Prefer this for reacting to a run when exact intermediate output is not needed.

variant.name: code-structure
variant.hypothesis: Explicitly guide code results toward outline or focus when the agent is orienting or locating identifiers, while reserving full or relevant for exact edits and body-level work to improve code savings without harming edit recall.

variant.name: conservative-body-expansion
variant.hypothesis: Require explicit block-level need before expanding code bodies, keeping signatures for orientation and identifier lookup to improve code savings while preserving exact-edit handling.

prompts.expandInstructions: The agent working on `task` just read this file (`agent.args`) for the reason in `agent.text_before_call`. Will the agent's immediate next step require the full body of block `blocks[{i}]`, rather than its signature, for editing, copying, or reasoning about its implementation?
prompts.expandTrue: Expand this block only because the task explicitly requires changing, copying, debugging, or explaining its implementation or exact behavior.
prompts.expandFalse: Keep this block collapsed when the agent only needs structure, available definitions, identifier locations, call relationships, or general orientation.

variant.name: command-default-signals
variant.hypothesis: Make signals the default for large command output unless the agent explicitly needs exact lines, while retaining structure-focused code views to increase savings without harming edit recall.

prompts.viewInstructions: A coding agent working on `task` just called `agent.tool` with `agent.args` (its reasoning right before the call is `agent.text_before_call`). Choose the smallest view that supports the agent's immediate next step. variant.name: code-relevant-threshold
variant.hypothesis: Clarify that code body inspection should use relevant while discovery should use outline or focus, reducing unnecessary full-code views without sacrificing edit recall.
